items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: I got this tuning from Patato Valdez

ctx.x: I do see. So if you did that specific song then the rest of the band is playing in C also on purpose?

No, no, no, no, no. It’s only for the conga player, for me just to have, I can’t tune to every key of every song so, but this is following the law of my default on tuning the drums with the G and C, this is only obvious or compatible notes that I can play within the G and C. I put the B flat, C, C7, and that’s going to have to go with everything for the night. I did one time tune to each different key on a recording, for a recording. I had time you know, what key is this in — give me the four notes and I would…

Okay. Have there been tunes that have come along that you feel like pop hits — let me go back. Jazz musicians, when, like Kenny G came out, most of them were like sort of disgusted at what he was doing. I think it shouldn’t have been called jazz in the first place. But at any rate, like a tune like the Macarena in ’97, do those kinds of sort of novelty Latin hits bother you?
